content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against its support: the account-page outage and the worst-minute failure rate both trace back to the figures and the cause, and the setting that was switched off is backed by the first paragraph. I'm now on the estimate of what the shop lost, and that line is cut off.

I'm going through the remaining claims one by one: the customer-loss estimate is supported, nobody was paged so no on-call time was spent, and the monthly-spend setting was switched back on, which is consistent with the revert. The legacy-checkout-fallback change ended the failures and is still in place, and the proposed code fix is only a draft that hasn't been applied.

supported.quote: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop could not load their account pages
rows: What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load

supported.quote: at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests failed
rows: Requests failing at the worst minute: 37.5% {peak_error_rate}

supported.quote: Someone had turned off a setting that kept account pages on their older version.
That sent shoppers to a newer version that likely breaks when it works out an average of this month's spending for anyone who has bought nothing this month.
Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 8,241.24 USD {customer_loss}

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, so the incident took no on-call time.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one

supported.quote: It first turned off a different setting, monthly-spend-feature, but that did not help, so Argus switched it back.
Argus then turned the account-page setting, legacy-checkout-fallback, back on. That ended the failures, and the setting is still on.
Argus has also proposed a code fix, but it is only a draft and has not been applied.
rows: Argus: proposed a fix, PR #525 - opened as a draft
The record holds nothing about it after that.
